Author: @Narcissa-o5c
Content:
UA came at an amazing time because we all needed a distraction during those times. It was fun, it was hilarious, and it was so heartbreaking when the timer hit zero and all I saw was my reflection staring back at me from the other side of my screen. Even with that, I'm still grateful to have had something to look forward to every day during a time when I couldn't really leave my house.

What makes revisiting the channel even more bittersweet, and what really hurts, is the fact that _all_ of my UA merch was in a box in a self storage unit that was absolutely demolished in the hurricane last year. I was, and still am, absolutely gutted to have lost all of that... It's not even the money that I spent on all of it that matters. It's the physical manifestation of those memories that I thought I would have forever only for them _all_ to be ripped away in a single night.

Author: @Lillylafrog
Content: I was really struggling with mental health in 2018 and would spend way too long on youtube so coming into 2019 I decided to quit entertainment online for a while. Unfortunately that happened to be during the year of Unus Annus. The last few days of Unus Annus, all my friends were talking about it. My friends were shocked that I didn't know what it was especially because I've always been a big fan of Markiplier, and I booted up YouTube for the first time in about a year to watch some of these videos. I made it through as many as I could, but only made it through a few because my mental health still was quite bad and just having enough energy to get enough homework in to pass (half) of my classes tore me apart, and I couldn't stop stressing about all I needed to do to the point I was paralyzed. All the stress had led me to want to kill myself. I ended up watching the stream for the end of Unus Annus and it just filled me with a hope and a vision that life is beautiful, that I still have time to create lasting memories and live a meaningful life. I talked at school about Unus Annus and made a friend that I still hold close to my heart. One time, when I was really struggling, they went on a walk and told me something I'll never forget "Things will get better. I really mean that, it might take 5 years and it might take 20, but I know you can see it though." I'm so glad Unus Annus could be a part of my life and help me find support in people I trust. Thank you PS. They were right, things have gotten better for me. I'm a better person and I'm feeling a lot better. I'm going through a little roadblock as I just graduated from a programming program at my local tech collage and I'm going to get thorough this part of life, I just have to give it the time and energy it needs. Thanks again to those who believed in me when I didn't believe in myself

Author: @vlad5488
Content:
i was 12 years old when unus annus started and i had already had shitty problems. had my first shot of whiskey long beforehand and smoked more than enough cigarettes with school getting harder and my father getting more of a piece of shit by the day, and god forbid i remember something ever, so seeing and getting attached to this channel felt like planning my own funeral. and i wasnt there for every episode, sadly. but at the end of it, i was there. the entire 24 hours i was there in that stream, watching the clock tick down. i remember getting worried id be late because my science class with my favorite teacher, Ms. KJ, would end around the same time the stream started. being able to remember something like that matters more to me than even i think i could ever realize.
admittedly, it got even worse three years later when i got used, groomed, and gained a pill addiction, and then lost my dog 13 days after our birthday, since we shared one. but each time i lost something i would occasionally remember crying the hardest i ever had watching this entire thing end and i think thats what also helped me through all this. the idea of you two doing this everyday, 365 days, made me realize i could push on. i can always push on.
five years seem so short until you live them, everyday, and even though the shitty bits i dont regret it because i have the most wonderful man to love in my life and the dearest best friend i could get, along with my other dear friends. i will carry that dead channel through my entire life. i will always do my best to remember it. i hope you both know how much of a difference you have made in my life, and in others.

Author: @MrStreaty122
Content:
5 years… wow, it’s been a while.

When Unus Annus began in 2019, I was living with my girlfriend in our apartment in KC. 

When the lockdowns came and the dread set in, it was what kept us laughing even as our families got sick (thankfully none of our families died.)

When Unus Annus died, she was actively cheating on me with, and I’m not exaggerating, dozens of people and only a few months later tried to keep it secret by leaving me. Goes to show how well that worked given that I’m telling you about it now.

I thought I would marry her, but as it turns out she had been using me the entire time we were together. 3 years dating, and almost 9 as friends, memories from almost half of my life with her in one way or another completely destroyed and tainted.

I’ve been rebuilding ever since. I moved out of that shitty apartment she dumped me in, upgraded my car twice, bought a house, lost 70 lbs, moved up in my career, became financially independent in that I don’t rely on anyone else for support, in short I’ve become a better man. 

Every so often I find a compilation of the old videos and reminisce on the bliss of ignorance. Spent a couple hours watching them last night actually. When I do watch them, I laugh of course, I’m reminded that I can’t let myself be used again. 

I had no idea this stream happened, it took 5 days for Youtube to tell me about it. 

Mark, I’ve been a subscriber of yours since your channel had only 150,000 subs oh so long ago. Watching your growth over the last 10+ years has been incredible, and congrats on getting married! I didn’t know about that either, it’s about goddamn time!

Author: @Cravenfishes
Content:
Unus Annus meant so much to me. Unus Annus was with me when i graduated, got my first job, moved out, found new friends, lost old friends, and ultimately, when i started finding myself. In all honesty, Unus Annus helped me become who i am today. The message that it gave, i repeat constantly, "life is short, and things arent going to be here forever. Dont be afraid to just do things, even if its not your best, even if it seems stupid to everyone else. If you want to do it, or if you love it, just go for it." Its helped me get through so much in my life, even right now, where my life seems to just be going out of control, i still think of it. 


Mark, Ethan and Amy will always be in my heart for this. I hope Mark knows that i see that he cares, that he puts his all into everything he does. He so often stretches himself thin, and i hope to everything that he knows we care, and we dont hold it against him when he needs to rest. 

Ethan, god I remember the backflip, and his rise to fame, me being just a kid when it all happened made me so happy, and it cave me confidence as well. Ethan, being this goofy guy, went and just did something, and ultimately it skyrocketed his career, and friend circle, that it gave me the confidence and the belief that maybe, if i was just myself, i could do it to. I think many people forget how impressionable things are on kids, but ill never forget how these guys impacted me when i was young. 

And Amy, man, anytime i see you, or more so hear you, it makes me so happy. Hearing you on Unus Annus was always such a treat, because you added so much life and humor to whatever Mark and Ethan were doing. And without a doubt if you werent there, Unus Annus would not have felt the same at all. I dont know if you know Amy but, god your so damn funny 😂 you are amazing, and such an integral part of how and why Unus Annus changed me. And to be honest, i dont think Unus Annus would have had all those amazing ideas, videos, vive, or hell, Unus Annus may not even had become a thing if you werent there! So i hope you know how much you have also impacted us Amy. 

At the end of the day, i always hear you guys say thank you to us, but i really really want to say to you guys.... thank you. Thank you so much for helping younger me become who i am. For being here for me on my worst days, my best days, and every other day that are just there to remind me im getting older. I dont think i would have become this person if it wasnt for you three, so thank you so much. You guys will always be my rocks, people who i will watch even if i make it to 80 years old, i will continue to watch you guys, to laugh when you laugh, cry when you cry, feel joy when you are happy, excitement when you start something new, and be proud when you pull off something amazing. So thank you from the bottom of my heart, for just waking up one day and deciding to do this. 

We love you, Mark, Amy, and Ethan. 🤍🩶🖤

Content: When Unus Annus originally happened, I had no home internet or electeonics of my own, save for a chromebook lent to me by my school. I tried to watch it but I never got to see more than a single video maybe two. I was upset about it for like three years where even thinking about it would make me so frustrated and sad that I'd missed out on something that seemed so cool. I think I managed to find a way to pop in for the last few minutes of the final stream? If there was one? I can't remember well, but having been there for the end was the only relief I had to missing out. Obviously, I was a little dramatic, it wasn't world-ending, I survived, but I felt so lost and excluded. I saw all the awesome fan art and the community it had, and I wanted in so badly. Even though I don't go crazy at the mention of Unus Annus anymore, and I've mostly come to terms with it, I still feel some sort of relief now, seeing this. Although, maybe some of the old anxiety is returning, just a smidgeon.

Author: @thatrandomvideoguy98
Content:
Towards the end of Unus Annus, I had a very old Basset Hound named Otis. He was sick, basically terminal. I was getting more and more into Unus Annus when he was getting worse and worse in health. He was my childhood. He was my life. He was there as a buddy to my first dog, Copper, and there through basically my entire life at that point, until the very end. I wanna say we had to put him down in the last couple of weeks, maybe the month leading up to the finale of Unus Annus. I remember I worked for a portion, but was able to make the final moments, the last few hours of Unus Annus. When I watched the craziness unfold, the channel and the chats and fan pages were all going crazy in a lot of different ways, I kept thinking about my, at the time, recently gone dog. How he kind of, lived his last year with Unus Annus being around. I know it means nothing to anyone else, least of all, Markiplier and Ethan. But, I remember trying to make a letter to each of you, as Unus and Annus, trying to thank you about being there when I was going through all of that. Unfortunately, I had that on a different laptop that has long since been battered and otherwise gone. I hope you guys know, that in all of that craziness, you made at least one person feel.... Weirdly at peace with his life at that point. And, while, at times I have struggled to live the life of a true Unus Annus soldier, I am ensuring the memories, though they may fade, still inspire. Still hold myself up. Still keep me accountable to try. 

So, to both Ethan and Mark
The deceased Unus and Annus
I thank you from all that I can, for all that you did, all that you desire, and all that you continue to do
from,
a random fan

Honestly, living through Unus Annus was like a fever dream. I was in Year 7 when it started, one of the worst years of my life due to bullying and not knowing who I was or wanted to be. Unus Annus filled a gap in my day, where I'd come home from school and I'd sit and brood. I'd get to come home to an episode and make sure I wasn't always upset. 

A few months before it had ended, my Dad died from cancer. And that was hard to deal with, even with family. Not many of them cared. But again, Unus Annus was there to give me the notice that nothing will last forever, and the memories and living in the moment are the most important things to ever do. 

Thank you, Mark, Ethan and Amy
And special thanks to the dogs too: Henry, Spencer and Chica. 

Thank you for making my life just that little bit better.

Life is different. The world is worse, though my 20 year old self would find that hard to imagine. And during these years I’ve held the memories of unus annus close (while wearing my last day merch ofc lol). I’m forever grateful to Mark for starting his channel. And after 12 years of being his biggest fan, with a lifetime left to go, I can say that he has helped me through so much that he’ll never know about.
Much love to anyone who reads this💞May you find peace and blessings in abundance

Content: I got the black hoodie and shirt, and one day me and my family and a couple of my sisters friends went awimming at a lake. There was a rocky outcropping maybe 30 or 40 feet from the shore. I was wearing my long sleeve unus annus shirt. We all decided to swim to the rocks, and i did it no problem. Then they wanted to swim back right away, so i naturally wanted to follow. They all got to the shore in no time, but i only got halfway when i stopped moving. I started bobbing in the water with an equal distance between the rocks and me, and me and the shore. My sister asked if i was good and i barely heard her, but all i could give was a thumbs down as i kept going under the water, there being only a foot or so between my feet and the lake bed. My sister swam over to me with the other two and were able to keep me above water long enough for us to inch to the shore. I swallowed a lot of water, and when i finally stood up, i fell over right away. All my muscles were completely shot. Ah memories

Unus Annus happened in a very difficult time in my life. It is what kept me alive, because I didn’t want to act on my inner thoughts and miss the next episode of Unus Annus, or especially the ending. It is what kept me going because I wanted to be a part of that, and it was all I felt I had in that year. When it ended, I was still in a rough place, but I kept going, and I’m still here. Sure, maybe I would have found another reason if Unus Annus didn’t happen, but it did, and it was my reason then to continue, and that will always mean a lot to me. 

Now, my life has turned around completely in the best way, and I am healing, and healthier than ever. Things got better significantly, and I know that I will never be in that same dark place ever again, nor will I ever consider cutting my life short. I have passions, and goals, and dreams, that I want to do in my life now before I die. I don’t want to die with regret that I didn’t do what I was passionate about doing, or even worse, regret that I didn’t even try. I have a passion for life now. ❤

Content: Unus Annus gave me a reason to keep going each day. I became really sick, then BLM, and felt so incredibly isolated during 2020. Each day, I'd go "2pm, you have to see it. 2pm." Thankfully, my mental well-being is a lot better now. However, I hope y'all really know just how much those videos helped many of us feel connected and gave us a source of free and accessible and HEALTHY escapism. Videos were five minutes to an hour. Every minute counted. Thank you. I'm not even done with this video, but I just wanted to share this.

Content:
Five years after Unus Annus ended, and just this year I've finally escaped my abuslve family and moved in with friends like I've been dreaming of for years, had the cops called on me twice by said parents, been stalked, and started testosterone and my transition 🏳️‍⚧️.  
Life moved so excruciatingly slow for so long, and suddenly things I'd been so inconsolably depressed over all the years I had to wait for them, (which ended up being nearly half my life) have finally happened, and I can finally start making progress with my life and picking up the pieces.

Some of the last times I felt like a person were during the pandemic playing minecraft with friends and sharing videos and hyperfixations. I remember how pretty much everyone I knew was sad when unus annus died, and us bonding over such a peculiar sense of grief. They've all drifted off by now, but i miss then a lot. Hopefully I'll relearn how to make friends eventually in any way other than trauma bonding.

Thank you guys.

Author: @LitLeo5260
Content:
The Unnus to my Annus left, but im still here. 

Ngl, that was my first thought, watching the stream. My older sister live with me and my fiancée during UA's year, and we watched almost every video together, some of them multiple times. We were there before and during the stream, we cried when it ended, and dressed up with the artwork she made for the ending, taking pictures and everything. We never did stuff like that together, not since we were kids. And then she left during the 5 years UA was dead, telling anyone who would listen that my partner and I are terrible-not going into details tho, thats just drama- and our older sister was one of the people that blindly listened. I dont even talk to either of them anymore because its always them wanting me to apologize for a list of things that never happened, or them needing financial support, and not once has it been anything else-even on my birthday and Christmas. 

Unnus annus gave me so much hope though. It was the last thing we really did together, where we didnt argue, or sit in silence, or just struggle in some way. Yeah, it gave me something to miss, but it also gave me one last thing to share with her as adults, before it came to that point of no return. I dont know how many times I cried watching the stream, thinking back on the time we shared and the time since, but God, I dont think I even let myself grieve her and the fact that she threw away how close we were as kids, how long we had only each other as company, and what all we went through together. I miss her. So much. But just like I knew you guys weren't done, weren't truly gone, i know she is. She's not going to come back any time soon, and I know shes not likely to have a genuine conversation or relationship with me again. But I also think I can actually grieve that now, now that this made me stop ignoring my feelings about it, or just staying angry.

Author: @aidenharkrider8132
Content:
While everyone else got to experience UA at such a critical time, I did too, but unfortunately for me, I was borderline suicidal with COVID, online learning, and quite literally having to be cooped up in my room due to renovations (we didn't have a livable first floor, and we dont have a full second floor by design--literally L shaped)

I was able to watch a decent amount, but I wasn't able to keep up. And, because I was not medicated at the time, that in of itself gave me stress and I pretty much had a huge shutdown that year. I dont blame myself, it was rough, but I do regret not having been able to catch more videos. I've been able to see some familiar and unfamiliar bits through fan compilations, but I don't dare look for any kind of archive. I have to live with my choices since life does not give you much courtesy to have a miraculous second chance. What's done is done, the clock has been dead for 5 years.

I think both UA and Frieren capture the feeling of "passing nostalgia" (if those words make much sense). The entire point for both is cherishing memory as time flies by, Frieren simply shows it on a much broader scale. I don't think enough media as a whole does this enough.

Author: @jamez6398
Content:
I prefer A Heist with Markiplier than In Space with Marikiplier... 

Iron Lung isn't a comedy? That's unexpected, I feel like even the video game is more, like, gameplay and atmosphere orientated than something super gritty like Doki Doki Literature Club or Mouthwashing, but I guess, then again, it's not a comedy either, although I still doubt it will be as brutal as the other comedy YouTubers turned serious horror movie co-directors RackRacka making Talk to Me and Bring Her Back, not that horror has to be the harshest vibe possible, execution is the only thing that matters. 

I do find it intriguing how many YouTubers are turning their hand to some really surprising productions of professionally produced looking horror movies recently, with how better that turns out now than the average person's ordinary expecations there lies, I find it interesting what draws so many specifically to the genre of horror? Very intriguing question. I think if I was a YouTuber who decided to make a professionally produced feature length movie production, I think I would rather make a moody thriller that gets really sad, upsetting, and traumatising due to conflict between people rather than an outright horror movie, but still boundary pushing with the harshness of its content, story, visuals, and effects, obviously.

Yeah, apparently, they were able to keep morale high on the set of No Country for Old Men, somehow, and that's one of the bleakest, most hopeless, and nihilistic movies ever made where everyone hurt each other and self-destructed due to abandoning their morality for the sake of petty greed and where no one gets a happy ending, not even the bad guys, to the point of being practically misanthropic. Unless if it just gets to the point whereby levity on set becomes almost a survival mechanism to withstand the nihilism of the movie, but, regardless, it was apparently a very fun shoot despite the end product being anything but. 

Doing a need instead of a want is always harder. I mean, it's easy for me to make YouTube videos, play video games, or watch YouTube than it is for me to brush my teeth, to brush my teeth is a mental hurdle that is nearly impossible to overcome for me, self-care is so monumentally strenuous to motivate myself to do. Doing things I want is so, so much easier to do, even if it's hard. 

Starting and finishing a project are the easiest parts of the project to enjoy and motivate yourself to do. It's when you're really, really far away from both the start and the end, in a massively, endless abyss of the middle and you can't see the end of the middle anywhere in sight as it stretches out past the horizon on all sides is the bit that's the hardest and most gruelling, especially the longer and longer you're trapped there for, especially when you get trapped in an endless cycle of setback after setback and end up making zero progress for a really, really long time despite spending 70 hours working on it just to see 0 progress due to the setbacks. Short-term projects are easier for that reason. If it's too short, it's not satisfying because you didn't put enough effort into it to get the dopamine out, but if it's short but not too short, that's best. When I set a short project to spend 20 hours on, then it somehow spirals out of control and I end up spending 200 hours on it when it's essentially just a hobby and I'm supposed to be doing things that fulfil the necessities of life that are not fulfilling, I get very, very heavily dismayed by that. 

I've had things that have no fixed deadline and no fixed goals of when to finish certain bits by, and I've grown to hate that over time because then you never get anything done when you can just keep putting it off forever and ever. I think my lack of self-discipline makes me never want to have to do freelance work, I think I need to be brutally forced into committing to finishing something by a certain deadline, and have short deadlines for small parts in between rather than some far-off deadline years and years into the future. 

Yeah, I hate when I'm trying to joke with my friends and they take me seriously and they get offended not because the joke is offensive but because they think I'm being completely serious and, because they're so defensive about their ability to tell whether somebody else is joking or not, they basically point blank refuse to accept the fact I was joking and it brings down the mood drastically. 

Once you gotten Iron Lung outta your system, you should really consider taking a break and going back to making regular YouTube content again instead for at least 6 months to a year before you go onto the next humongous project.

Content:
"People that were in highschool arent in high school anymore" literally gave me weird chills. I just finished college (in AUS, college is yr 11 and 12), so yes. I started high school, year 7, with Unus Annus, and now I've left college, year 12, with the 5th anniversary.

Thinking back to that time, i was so naïve, but I didn’t know it. Mark basically raised me, as i have emotionally disconnected parents, as well as Autistic barriers that make life difficult — he was always THE youtuber i looked forward to during primary school. His fnaf videos MADE ME. They SHAPED ME as a person. Now, seeing how much he, Ethan, and even my perception of Amy, have changed, it makes me realise "Fuck. Things have happened. Everything has changed, as you watched, and you didnt know." I mean, i did know, but realising life has gone on and on and on, despite roadblocks, has been such a punch in the gut. 

Im off to University next year, i have a casual job, i have connections, im in therapy... IM AN ADULT. Ive grown from that little weird kid, intona delightfully weird adult. Five years was enough change to become confident, to find my place, and with that.... im really exited to see what endeavours five years of building to has accomplished.

I love you Mark, the one adult i coukd always count on to keep me grounded. I love you Ethan, for being so inspiring with your growth. And Amy, you seem to be the glue to everything, which is so important.

🤍⌛️Memento Mori ⌛️🖤

Author: @cryptidinthecloset6912
Content:
I remember just, sitting in my room up late— only one awake in my house, tears in my eyes watching that year countdown to midnight at its end. I wasn’t bawling, just teary eyed. When everything finally ended I sat in my room in the dark for an hour just existing. Didn’t cry, didn’t speak, didn’t move just felt for a while. I don’t even remember going to sleep.

I would love to rewatch UA, but even when I see reuploads of the “best bits” something stops me, it was supposed to be that once it’s gone, it’s gone.

Loved to live it, love to see it, love to look back.

Content:
i remember so well that i wanted to be there the whole last stream, but being in Italy meant it was already late when it began; when i woke up the channel was already gone. i also remember wearing my black and white barista three-piece suit AT HOME to commemorate the channel (my mom was so weirded out LMFAO). still though, i got a couple compilation videos in my (very autistic) mega playlist.

love all of you guys 🤍🤍🤍🤍

The start, with Mark rolling out of the coffin, that was BEAUTIFULLY choreographed. In addition to that, having Mark be slower and having Ethan be faster makes it so the sequence makes so much more sense, with Ethan "hurrying" Mark (when in reality, it's just a stage maneuver to avoid risk). Just, magnificent work, guys. Seriously. Gorgeous.

Content:

I have my Unus Annus poster on my wall, I wear my coffin and zeros shirts all the time, the hourglass YooTooz sits on my shelf, and I still sleep in my now tattered up Unus Annus hoodie. This channel changed my life and it’s one of my many blessings that I got to be there for every video. Soon I’ll be getting my first Tattoo, the hourglass, the zeros, the phrase. Memento Mori. Unus Annus. 

Unus Annus taught more than just “life is short.” It came into my life when I most wanted to give up and showed me that I had to carry on. 

Thank you
🖤🤍

Content:
Unus Annus certainly meant a lot to me, as it was active during a particularly rough patch in my life. I was a shipping factory worker, nearly hating my day to day cause it didn't pay enough to sustain independent living conditions. But I still remember during my time in the breakroom being able to watch the daily Unus Annus videos and getting joy out of watching them. I'd always be eagerly awaiting the next video whenever I'd get to the break room day to day. I even got so motivated to participate that I submitted a video for one of the challenge videos you guys did from time to time (I'm one of the Polar Plunge winners you guys picked, still have the hoodie and autographed sticker hanging around!)

Sadly I missed out on the final days, as the death of Unus Annus happened right as I joined boot camp for Navy. I actually just celebrated my own 5 year anniversary of being in the military just yesterday, and I've done so much better since those rougher times 5 years ago. I just wanna say to everyone that helped and worked on this project with y'all that this certainly meant a lot to me, and I thank y'all for making Unus Annus - probably wouldn't where I am today without those videos keeping me sane and motivated.

Author: @pidge_bites

I'm so grateful I got to catch this live. Since then my life is completely different. I came out, fully transitioned, I have an entirely different social circle of amazing people around me, and I'm engaged. I watched the goodbye stream in an apartment I'd moved into after a bad breakup that happened during the life of the channel, and tonight I watched the anniversary stream while recovering from top surgery, in a new city, in a new apartment that I share with my fiance.

The nostalgia I hold for UA is strong, and I got surprisingly emotional over this stream. It was nice to just spend time with you three again and to hear new perspectives and reminisce about the channel. Thank you for all the laughs and the good times. Memento Mori.
